transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been having trouble going to the toilet. I'm opening my bowels much less often than usual, and when I do I have to strain quite hard.
When did you first notice it?
It started about three weeks ago. It's been getting worse since then.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
I've been drinking less than I used to — maybe three cups of tea a day — because I don't want to keep getting up in the night. I think that's made it worse.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
The stools are hard and come out in little pellets, and the straining is uncomfortable — I'd say about a 4 out of 10. My lower tummy also feels bloated.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's my lower tummy that feels bloated. No, it doesn't spread anywhere else.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
The straining is about a 4 out of 10 — uncomfortable, but not the worst pain I've known.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
The bloating seems to be there most of the time. The straining happens when I try to go — and that's now only about every four or five days, whereas normally I'd go every day or every other day.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
No, nothing else like that — no blood in the stools, no black stools, and I haven't been sick. Just the bloating and the straining.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes. I have arthritis in my spine and my knees, and I have an irregular heartbeat — atrial fibrillation.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I take several. About a month ago I started co-codamol 30/500, two tablets four times a day, for back pain. I also take apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day, bisoprolol 2.5 mg once a day, and a calcium and vitamin D chewable tablet twice a day.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, I don't have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Not really — I still get about and do my usual things at home. It's more just uncomfortable than stopping me doing anything.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Well, I'd like something to get things moving again, that's the main thing. But I must admit I do worry it could be something serious — like bowel cancer.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
